name: Pocahontas
kicker: Daughter of Chief Powhatan · Her marriage brought peace to Jamestown
briefing: Pocahontas was a childhood nickname meaning something like “playful one,” given to a daughter of Powhatan, the chief whose people lived around Jamestown. Captured by the English in 1613, she became a Christian named Rebecca, married the tobacco planter John Rolfe, and sailed to England, where she met King James I and died in 1617. Disney’s 1995 movie made her John Smith’s girlfriend, but that romance never happened.
answerHtml: Pocahontas (accept Matoaka or Amonute; accept Rebecca Rolfe before “Rebecca” is read; prompt on Rolfe alone)

sample.note: 7 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (5 Middle School/Easy High School + 2 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: Virginia’s Racial Integrity Act of 1924 included an exception named for this woman, because many powerful Virginia families claimed to descend from her. Captain Samuel Argall captured this woman in 1613 and held her for ransom at Henricus.
tossups.r: She later married John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this daughter of Chief Powhatan who, according to legend, saved John Smith’s life.

tossups.p: This woman and a priest named Tomocomo watched a royal masque at Whitehall Palace and met King James I. About two months later, this woman fell ill and died at Gravesend just as her ship was starting the voyage home to Virginia.
tossups.r: She had come to England with her husband, John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this Powhatan woman who, legend says, rescued John Smith.

tossups.p: The minister Alexander Whitaker taught this young woman about Christianity while she was held captive at Henricus, a settlement up the James River from Jamestown. After her baptism, she took a new English name.
tossups.r: That name was Rebecca. For 10 points, name this daughter of Chief Powhatan who married the colonist John Rolfe.

tossups.p: Some historians believe this woman had married a Powhatan warrior named Kocoum before the English captured her. Her later wedding to an English tobacco planter began about eight years of peace that were named after her.
tossups.r: That planter was John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this Native American woman who, the story goes, saved Captain John Smith.

tossups.p: A Patawomeck leader and his wife helped Captain Samuel Argall lure this young woman onto an English ship in 1613. The English then held her for ransom, demanding that her father free English prisoners and return stolen weapons.
tossups.r: During her captivity, she became a Christian. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who married John Rolfe.

tossups.p: Simon van de Passe made the only portrait of this woman drawn from life, a 1616 engraving that shows her dressed in fine English clothes. In London, this woman was introduced to high society as “Lady Rebecca.”
tossups.r: As a girl, she had visited the fort at Jamestown. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who, legend says, saved John Smith’s life.

tossups.p: John Gadsby Chapman’s painting of this woman’s baptism hangs in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol. That painting shows this woman kneeling as she becomes a Christian and is given the name Rebecca.
tossups.r: Her husband, John Rolfe, made tobacco Virginia’s money crop. For 10 points, name this daughter of Chief Powhatan.

tossups.p: After Opechancanough [“oh-puh-CHAN-kuh-noh”] captured an English explorer in 1607, he brought his prisoner to Werowocomoco [“wair-uh-wuh-KOH-muh-koh”]. There, the explorer later claimed, this girl laid her head on his to stop warriors from executing him.
tossups.r: That explorer was John Smith. For 10 points, name this daughter of Chief Powhatan who later married John Rolfe.

tossups.p: John Smith’s first written account of his capture did not mention this girl saving him. He told that famous story years later, most fully in his 1624 _Generall Historie of Virginia_, after this woman had died, so many historians doubt it.
tossups.r: She took the name Rebecca after becoming a Christian. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who, legend says, rescued Smith.

tossups.p: This woman’s son, Thomas, was born in 1615 and was raised in England after she died there. First Lady Edith Wilson was one of the many Virginians who descended from that son.
tossups.r: His father was the tobacco planter John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who, legend says, saved John Smith.

tossups.p: This woman’s best-known name was really a childhood nickname meaning something like “playful one.” As a girl, she often visited the English fort on the James River, bringing food and messages from her father’s people.
tossups.r: Her father was Powhatan. For 10 points, name this woman who married John Rolfe and took the name Rebecca.

tossups.p: This woman’s husband grew a sweeter kind of tobacco from seeds that came from Spanish colonies, creating Virginia’s first big money crop. Their 1614 wedding began years of calm between the English colonists and her people.
tossups.r: A 1995 Disney movie wrongly made her John Smith’s love interest. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who married John Rolfe.

tossups.p: While this woman was held at Henricus, a widowed planter wrote a long letter to Sir Thomas Dale asking permission to marry her. Her father, who had not met all of the English ransom demands, agreed to the match.
tossups.r: That planter was John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this Powhatan woman who was baptized as Rebecca.

tossups.p: A statue of this woman stands at St. George’s Church in Gravesend, England, where she was buried in 1617. The Virginia Company had paid for her trip to England to help attract new investors and settlers to its colony.
tossups.r: She traveled with her husband, John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who, legend says, saved John Smith.

tossups.p: When this woman met John Smith again near London, she had been told for years that he was dead. Smith wrote that she turned away and hid her face before she would speak to him.
tossups.r: She was visiting England with her husband, John Rolfe. For 10 points, name this daughter of Powhatan who supposedly saved Smith’s life back in Virginia.

trap.title: Disney Isn’t History
trap.body: Disney’s 1995 movie shows a grown-up Pocahontas falling in love with John Smith. In real life she was about 11 when they met, there was no romance, and the Englishman she married was John Rolfe. Real tossups skip the movie and use her capture, her baptism as Rebecca, and her trip to England, so a player who only knows the film may freeze. She also shows up as a clue in tossups about Powhatan, John Smith, John Rolfe, and Jamestown.
trap.fix: Rolfe, Rebecca, Henricus, Samuel Argall, or a trip to England means Pocahontas. If “Pocahontas” is read out loud as a clue, the answer is someone else, such as her father Powhatan, John Smith, or John Rolfe. Don’t mix her up with Sacagawea, the Shoshone woman who guided Lewis and Clark nearly 200 years later.
trap.line: Real answer line: Pocahontas (accept Matoaka or Amonute; accept Rebecca Rolfe before “Rebecca” is read; prompt on Rolfe alone)
